requirements.text: REQ-VALID-ANSWERED: every valid check is answered with granted or denied.
REQ-INVALID-NOOP: every invalid check is rejected and leaves the state unchanged.
REQ-EFFECTS: an answered check leaves the users and the access list unchanged and appends exactly one log record with its decision.
REQ-DEFAULT-DENY: without a matching allow entry, access is not granted.
REQ-DENY-OVERRIDES: a matching deny entry at least as specific as every matching allow entry prevents access.

witness.message: granted although a deny entry is at least as specific as every allow

requirements.text: REQ-SPECIFIC-ALLOW: a valid check is granted when a matching allow entry is strictly more specific than every matching deny entry.

witness.message: a strictly more specific allow entry matches, but access was denied

requirements.text: REQ-GRANT-JUSTIFIED: a granted check has a matching allow entry strictly more specific than every matching deny entry.

witness.message: granted without a strictly more specific allow entry

requirements.text: REQ-ORDER-INDEPENDENT: reordering the access list does not change any outcome.

witness.message: follow-up case: reversed entries give denied, original order gave granted

requirements.text: REQ-DENIAL-EXPLAINED: a denied check has no matching allow entry, or a matching deny entry at least as specific as every matching allow entry.

witness.message: denied without a covering deny entry

trust_assumptions: Lean v4.35.0 kernel, compiler and runtime
the protected spec and locked challenge as reviewed by the owner
the executable wrapper (app/Main.lean) is TESTED_ONLY, not proved
scope: Properties are proved about the pure definitions step in namespace Acl for all inputs; the executable acl-sidecar is built from the same source and tested, and its JSON wrapper is not proved.

counterexamples.message: granted although a deny entry is at least as specific as every allow
counterexamples.lean_source:
import Solution
import Acl.Spec

/-!
Generated by harness/counterexample.py. Refutes `Acl.req_deny_overrides` (REQ-DENY-OVERRIDES) for the candidate's definitions
on the failing case

{"request": {"path": [2, 3, 1], "user": 5}, "state": {"entries": [["allow", 0, [2, 3]], ["deny", 0, [2, 3]]], "log": [[8, [3], false], [1, [2, 2], false]], "users": [7, 1, 5, 8]}}

the case's state and check
-/

set_option maxRecDepth 100000
set_option maxHeartbeats 20000000

namespace Acl

theorem cex_req_deny_overrides : ¬ (DenyOverrides step) := by
  intro h
  have hx := h (({ users := ([7, 1, 5, 8] : List Nat), entries := ([⟨.allow, 0, ([2, 3] : List Nat)⟩, ⟨.deny, 0, ([2, 3] : List Nat)⟩] : List Entry), log := ([⟨8, ([3] : List Nat), false⟩, ⟨1, ([2, 2] : List Nat), false⟩] : List Record) } : State)) (({ user := 5, path := ([2, 3, 1] : List Nat) } : Request))
  first
    | (revert hx; decide)
    | (revert hx; decide +kernel)
    | (simp -failIfUnchanged only [ValidQuery, Matches, HasAllow, Overridden, Permitted, ValidAnswered, InvalidNoop, Effects, DefaultDeny, DenyOverrides, SpecificAllow, GrantJustified, OrderIndependent, DenialExplained] at hx <;> (revert hx; decide))
    | (repeat (first | exact absurd hx (by decide) | exact absurd hx.1 (by decide) | replace hx := hx.2); done)

end Acl
